new_direct_evidence.title: Core extensions for non-balanced TU-games
new_direct_evidence.access: Public author-uploaded full-text transcription accessible through web tool. ResearchGate labels content uploaded by Camelia Bejan on July 1, 2014.
new_direct_evidence.version_evidence: Displayed journal header Int J Game Theory (2009) 38:3–16, original-paper label, DOI, accepted 15 July 2008, published online 9 August 2008, Springer-Verlag copyright and journal page headers.
new_direct_evidence.pages_directly_compared: Section 2, printed pp.5–7; key expansion and efficient-payoff definitions and balanced-core statement on p.6. Surrounding tax-refinement definitions on p.7 inspected. Selected later context inspected, not a complete line-by-line article comparison.
new_direct_evidence.technical_paraphrase: For nonnegative TU games, X(v) consists of efficient vectors. T(v,x) minimizes nonnegative additions that cover excesses. T(v) minimizes this over X(v); EC(v) consists of minimizing efficient vectors. A nonempty original core gives T(v)=0 and EC(v)=C(v).
new_direct_evidence.comparison_inference: These published definitions agree with the previously inspected 2008 author version on the cited baseline. In the static manuscript the original game is already balanced; its positive expenditure comes from the extra frozen H/3 constraints. This scoped comparison neither supplies nor disproves the sharp class-specific subsidy theorem.
new_direct_evidence.scope_closed: Direct access/comparison of the cited definitions in published-layout text, rather than author-version-only evidence.
new_direct_evidence.scope_not_closed: Publisher PDF binary not obtained. Whole-paper word-for-word version audit and exhaustive implication/priority clearance not performed.

new_direct_evidence.download_result: Two ordinary web-tool download links gave Internal Error. A normal HTTPS page request returned HTTP403; stopped, no alternate headers/authentication/bypass.
